reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical designs: Structured Outputs with an enum, reason separated from category, a tagged ticket, explicit data-not-instructions rules and a 30-50 ticket eval. B pulls slightly ahead with concrete validation-and-fallback code covering JSON and refusal failures, more examples (including a pure-injection case that maps to other) and a detailed test table covering tag-closing injection, English input, empty input and long input, plus a separate injection accuracy metric. A is tighter but gives the code-side fallback only as a one-line .get suggestion.

B: Overstates that with the enum there will be no arbitrary text output after injection; the free-form reason field can still carry attacker-influenced text.
